idiom_name: Var/Signal owner as supply half; pure HtmlElement-building functions as the presentational half (Laminar/Airstream); Play action plus Twirl template server-side
implementation_notes: In Laminar/Airstream the reactive state is a value: whatever owns the Var or Signal is the supply half, and children are ordinary functions that build elements from the values and signals they are handed - there is no virtual DOM and no component instance, so a child really is a pure function of its input, which makes the presentational half the default rather than a discipline. Pass signals rather than plain values where the child must update (value <-- query, onInput --> query), and keep every mutation in the owner. Server-rendered Scala uses the same split through the framework: a Play action loads the data and a Twirl template receives it as explicit parameters, so the template renders its arguments and nothing else.
pitfalls: Holding reactive state outside its owner (a global Var, or a value captured beyond its lifetime) hides ownership and leaks subscriptions.
A two-way sink such as `onInput --> query` combined with a parent that also writes the same Var can loop; pick one writer per interaction path.
Rendering dynamic children without a keyed or split strategy recreates elements on every emission and loses focus and scroll position.
